data.credibility: Management frequently guides aggressive expansion across segments like IT and telecom, but several targets are dropped or quietly not mentioned in subsequent quarters. Capex targets are met reasonably well, though operational timelines like washing machine production have slipped.

lines.line: Camera modules volume targeted at 190 to 200 million units; ongoing status is on track.
Camera modules revenue of INR 6,000 to 7,000 crores was dropped from subsequent discussions.
Investment commitment of INR 3,000 crores for components was dropped after Q2 FY26.
IT business revenue target of Rs. 15,000 to 20,000 crores was raised; status remains on track.
IT products domestic market business target of $1.5 to $2 billion was dropped.
IT hardware revenue of INR 1,500 crores for FY26 was subsequently dropped.
Capex outgo for FY26 guided at INR 1,100 to 1,200 crores; delivered INR 1,058 crores.
Front-loading washing machine mass production start delayed to Q2 FY27.
Telecom segment revenue of INR 7,500 to 8,000 crores lowered then delayed, currently slipping.
Lighting segment revenue target of INR 1,700 crores in FY27 was dropped.
Camera module revenue target of INR 2,500 crores is on track.
Display module JV peak revenue target of INR 5,500 to 6,000 crores is on track.
Telecom segment revenue target revised to INR 6,700 to 7,000 crores; status pending.
IT hardware revenue expected to reach INR 6,000 crores in current fiscal; pending.
Vivo JV volume expected around 20 to 21 million next year; pending.
Q Tech revenue target for next year set at INR 2,500 to 3,000 crores; pending.
IT hardware capex commitment increased to INR 500 crores under IT PLI 2; pending.

bull: Revenue has compounded at 49.9% annually over five years, reaching a TTM figure of ₹58,523 crores with strong operating cash flows at 122% of profit.
Working-capital days have tightened from 9 to -3 over five years, demonstrating efficient capital conversion amid rapid growth.
Robust return metrics with ROE at 25.2% and ROCE at 29.2%, supported by a lightly geared debt-to-equity ratio of 0.21.
bear: EBITDA margins have compressed from 4.5% in FY21 to 3.8% in FY26, settling at a low 3.2% TTM.
High valuation with a P/E of 51.8 leaves little margin for error given thin operational margins.
Management frequently drops or revises specific multi-year revenue and investment targets, introducing execution uncertainty.
